text:
Mike H: quick sync — started a soft hedging run to see if small holdtime perturbations reduce oscillation when kernel selection flips. posting early notes.

Sana R: nice, what parameters are you sweeping?

Mike H: keeping base micro-batch interval at 2ms, coalesce delay mean 1.2ms, adding gaussian jitter sigma=0.4ms, and a soft-hedge that nudges holdtime by +/-0.6ms after two consecutive kernel swaps. token budget target still 1024 per batch.

Lee T: curious — are we changing queue priority behavior too or just holdtime?

Mike H: only holdtime/jitter for this run. queue policy left as current FIFO with priority buckets unchanged. want to isolate effect on KV priming and kernel thrash.

Julia M: perf-bot summaries from the first hour? :eyes:

perf-bot: [run 1764123456] epoch 1/6 completed, p50 +1.2ms, p95 +9ms vs baseline, kernel-swap-count reduced by 18% in shard A, KV-hit-rate stable at 94.1%.

Sana R: kernel-swap reduction is promising. but p95 +9ms worries me — where's the extra tail from?

Mike H: looked at traces — tail spikes align with batches that hit a cold KV set after we nudged holdtime down. small coalesces decreased batching for some mid-length sequences and caused more kernel boundary crossings.

Lee T: can you paste the perf snippet? would help to see stack / kernel selection traces.

Mike H: here's an anonymized extract from the trace:

```
trace 2024-06-12 10:32:11 shardA req=0x7f
  batch_size=3 seq_len=128 tokens=384
  selected_kernel=matmul_fuse_v2
  kv_lookup miss -> warm_kv_fill (12ms)
  kernel_swap -> matmul_v1 (swap cost 8ms)
  total_processing 34ms
```

Mike H: more often when holdtime nudged shorter we saw small batches skip into different kernel families (v2->v1) causing swap cost ~8ms which dominated tail.

Sana R: could we bias hedging only towards longer holdtimes so we avoid premature downsizing? i.e., asymmetric hedge +0.8ms / -0.2ms?

Mike H: good idea — will try asymmetric hedges next run. also plan to bump token budget target to 1536 for one arm to see if slightly larger batches mitigate kernel-crossing.

Julia M: also consider read-ahead KV priming on suspected hot keys for the small-batch path. cheap prefetch might remove the 12ms.

Lee T: agree — an inexpensive KV priming on first bucket join could help. but watch memory pressure. maybe limit priming to top-5 hot keys per shard.

perf-bot: FYI: current run 1764123456 has a config blob attached to experiment id exp-h-1764.

Mike H: config we used for this run:

```
{\n  "micro_batch_ms": 2.0,\n  "coalesce_mean_ms": 1.2,\n  "coalesce_jitter_sigma_ms": 0.4,\n  "holdtime_hedge": {"type": "symmetric", "delta_ms": 0.6, "trigger_swaps": 2},\n  "token_budget_target": 1024,\n  "queue_policy": "fifo_buckets",\n  "kv_priming": "none"\n}
```

Sana R: next steps I propose: 1) asymmetric hedging (+0.8/-0.2), 2) token budget arm at 1536, 3) KV priming top-5 hot keys on small-batch path. run arms for 3h each.

Lee T: SGTM. add a metric for "kernel_swap_latency" (time spent in swap ops) and "post_swap_kv_miss" so we can correlate.

Mike H: will add those metrics and schedule runs later today. tagging @Julia M for KV priming implementation notes — any constraints on priming rate?

Julia M: can do priming with a leaky bucket limiter set to 50 priming ops/sec per shard, cap memory at 8MB per shard for primed entries. will push a patch.

perf-bot: queued experiments: exp-h-1764-asym, exp-h-1764-1536, exp-h-1764-kvprime. expected runtimes 3h each.

Mike H: thanks everyone. if any regressions show up I'll post p95/p99 diffs and flame graphs. :thumbsup:

Sana R: awesome — ping when first 3h results are in. :thinking:
